pr_body:
Fork of #14483, but [gave up MasterKey](https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/pull/14483#issuecomment-1350728557), and fixed some problems.

Close #12065.
Needed by #13539.

Featrues:
- Secrets for repo and org, not user yet.
- Use SecretKey to encrypte/encrypt secrets.
- Trim spaces of secret value.
- Add a new locale ini block, to make it easy to support secrets for user.

Snapshots:

Repo level secrets:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9418365/207823319-b8a4903f-38ca-4af7-9d05-336a5af906f3.png)

Rrg level secrets
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9418365/207823371-8bd02e93-1928-40d1-8c76-f48b255ace36.png)
pr_comments: I do like this PR more because it addresses my comment here https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/pull/14483#issuecomment-1279716834 👍

I would really like to see a docs page like https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/encrypted-secrets 

Could you please add the user secrets too? See https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/pull/21888 to not duplicate the logic.

> Could you please add the user secrets too? See https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/pull/21888 to not duplicate the logic.

I prefer to support user level secrets later, because it's only used by Actions right now, and there's no user level runner yet. So I think it makes senses to use another PR(s) to support both user runners and user secrets.

You know, it has blocked Actions for a long time, we need to move fast.

How about the docs? 🙂

The actions PR already uses the `routers/common` package to reduce the code duplication between users and organizations. Only the user routes missing at the moment I think.
The secret code does not distinguish between the owners:
https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/pull/21937/files#diff-cd4aa1f217c85f6ea341104754c4ad93b3526a2222cd14b8011180f3343c5462R44-R48

> How about the docs? 🙂

As lunny [said](https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/pull/14483#issuecomment-1279941185):

"Currently, the usage of UI is simple so I think it seems it's unnecessary."

And I'm sure it will be further refined soon, and it's a better time to write docs when it's stable.

> The actions PR already uses the `routers/common` package to reduce the code duplication between users and organizations. Only the user routes missing at the moment I think. The secret code does not distinguish between the owners: [#21937 (files)](https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/pull/21937/files#diff-cd4aa1f217c85f6ea341104754c4ad93b3526a2222cd14b8011180f3343c5462R44-R48)

Actually, it's never the route that is missing, but the design. Should we support user level secrets and runners when neither GitHub nor Gitlab supports it? Of course we don't need to follow them, but we need to know why.

> > How about the docs? 🙂
> 
> As lunny [said](https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/pull/14483#issuecomment-1279941185):
> 
> "Currently, the usage of UI is simple so I think it seems it's unnecessary."
> 
> And I'm sure it will be further refined soon, and it's a better time to write docs when it's stable.

The package registry has also a little UI and still the docs are valuable.

> Actually, it's never the route that is missing, but the design. Should we support user level secrets and runners when neither GitHub nor Gitlab supports it? Of course we don't need to follow them, but we need to know why.

Here is the usecase: https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/pull/14483#issuecomment-1348092108

Quote from the Github docs:
> Organization-level secrets let you share secrets between multiple repositories, which reduces the need for creating duplicate secrets. Updating an organization secret in one location also ensures that the change takes effect in all repository workflows that use that secret.

The same is true on the user level.

> The package registry has also a little UI and still the docs are valuable.

Take a look at package registry, there are some documents about how to use `docker` command to connect Gitea's docker registry.
But for current secrets UI, only `Add Secrets` and `Delete` two buttons. And maybe we could improve the documents when actions merged so that we can say the secrets could be used in `actions` as blabla. For now, I don't think we need an article to explain the two buttons and those secrets cannot be used anywhere else.

I think as a minimal one to support actions, this PR could be merged if there is no obvious problem and we could proposal more related PRs.

> Secret names must not start with the `GITHUB_` prefix.

Yeah, right, it probably makes sense to reserve a prefix for us as well, otherwise we might get some problems later on.
Handled it with what GitHub does:
I submit a document to describe the name rules, please help to confirm the document is consistent with the code.

Our Markdown docs linter complains about two spaces at the end of a line?
One of the two official ways of writing a newline?
Interesting…

I think this PR is ready to be inserted into the merge queue.
It has been scrutinized in depth by both @KN4CK3R and myself.
Nothing unimplemented we mentioned is blocking.
The remaining things can still be added later. (incorrect deletion dialogue text, user secrets, linking to the org secrets from the repo secrets settings)
So, if anyone notices something absolutely wrong, they should comment now.

issue_context.title: Personal Secrets store and Organization secrets store
issue_context.body:
When you want to migrate from a SSH or from a private Github repository, You have to input the token or private key to do that. A more convenient way is to store all the secrets on gitea and use them when needed.

For a self-hosted instance, we should store them as encrypted data. A random key could be saved on user table to encrypt/decrypt the data.

review_comments:
As I said on the previous PR:
I think it would be a good idea to add `ctx.Data["UserSecrets"] = FindSecrets(ctx, opts{OwnerID: ctx.Owner.ID})` (pseudo code)
so that we can also display read-only the user/org secrets that are already defined, and link to the corresponding settings page.
However, this can also be postponed for later if necessary.
I think it's a good idea, but let's do it later.
Alternatively, we could also delete by name, repo, and owner.
I'm not sure, maybe we can provide batch deletion later.

That wasn't what I meant:
I simply meant that deletion by id is certainly the easiest way to implement it, but we could also have implemented it by using the secret name, owner, and repo. That makes it at least for users easier to see that the correct secret will be deleted.
But it is such an unimportant detail that we can end this discussion now and keep the current approach.
@delvh While I agree with you, usually the user will never see this request because it is just a POST from the overview page. So the user will not see the called url.
Should `Secret.Validate()` check the max size too?
